  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: The keyword check uses substring matching, so a standalone keyword can be removed while a compound regex containing the same text still makes the test pass.
  WHY: The extracted alternation can still contain `token` or `secret` as substrings of `auth[_-]?token` / `client[_-]?secret`, so the redaction policy can lose a standalone entry without failing the test.
- tests/test_implement_post_codex_recovery.py:~1623-1665 | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_1-fast]
  PROBLEM: The alternation-extraction regex is tightly coupled to the exact awk formatting and can fail on harmless refactors.
  WHY: Small whitespace or shape changes to the awk expression can make the test unable to extract the alternation even when redaction behavior is unchanged.
- tests/test_implement_post_codex_recovery.py:~1744-1789 | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_1-fast]
  PROBLEM: The GH_TOKEN check slices the workflow text using a fixed `run: |` anchor and step ordering assumptions.
  WHY: A valid workflow refactor can change the step structure or `run:` style and make the test fail or inspect the wrong block.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

  WHY: `token` still matches `auth[_-]?token` and `secret` still matches `client[_-]?secret`, which can let a standalone redaction entry disappear without the test failing.
- tests/test_implement_post_codex_recovery.py:1637-1650 | confidence=2

  WHY: If the awk alternation ever contains a literal `)` in a keyword or pattern, the test would truncate the extracted alternation and report a confusing failure.
